audit.reasoning: Quote: confirmed verbatim in the freshly downloaded Kittel 1903 djvu text (§11, line 463), and confirmed to be the book's only accent statement; but no file had been held, so quote_check = no copy held to check with confirmation noted. Deciding source: a 1903 missionary/pedagogical grammar of literary Kannada based on the Sabdamanidarpana, one unargued sentence — far from the best available given Sridhar 1990 (Routledge reference grammar with a stress subsection) and Savithri 1995 (instrumental). Nothing I could open contradicts initial prominence: Schiffman 1979/1983 is silent but describes post-initial short-vowel deletion/reduction (p.19), and secondary reports of Sridhar 1990/Savithri 1995 describe stress as non-contrastive, weakly cued, with word-initial syllables most often perceived as prominent — all compatible with 'fixed-dominant initial'.
